questions.question: What is the primary objective of Incident Management in ServiceNow?

options.text: To identify the root cause of all service disruptions
To restore normal service operation as quickly as possible
To implement permanent fixes for all reported issues
To prevent all future incidents from occurring

explanation.correct: The primary goal of Incident Management is to restore normal service operation as quickly as possible, minimizing the adverse impact on business operations. This may involve applying temporary workarounds rather than permanent fixes. Root cause analysis is the responsibility of Problem Management.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Identifying root causes is the responsibility of Problem Management, not Incident Management
Incident Management focuses on service restoration, often using temporary workarounds. Permanent fixes are handled through Problem and Change Management
While reducing incidents is desirable, the primary focus of Incident Management is restoration, not prevention

source.excerpt: The main goal of incident management is to swiftly restore services without necessarily identifying the root cause. In other words, the focus is restoring services as soon as possible.

questions.question: Which incident state indicates that the service issue has been fixed but is waiting for user confirmation?

explanation.correct: The Resolved state indicates that the service issue has been fixed, but the system is waiting for the user to confirm that the service has been restored. After confirmation or a timeout period (default 7 days), the incident moves to Closed.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Closed means the incident is no longer active and has been fully completed
On Hold means the investigation is temporarily paused to gather additional information
In Progress indicates the incident has been assigned and is under active investigation

source.excerpt: Resolved means that the service issue has been fixed. But we're waiting for the user to confirm that the service has been restored.

questions.question: When does the SLA clock for incident resolution end?

options.text: When the incident is assigned to a group
When the incident state is set to Closed
When the incident state is set to Resolved
When the Assigned To field is populated

explanation.correct: The SLA clock for resolution ends when the state is set to Resolved. The response SLA ends when the Assigned To field is completed and state is In Progress, but the resolution SLA continues until Resolved.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Assignment to a group does not stop the resolution SLA clock
The resolution SLA ends at Resolved, not Closed. Closed is a final state after user confirmation
Populating the Assigned To field ends the response SLA, not the resolution SLA

source.excerpt: Once the Assigned To field is completed and the state is set to In Progress, the response SLA ends while the resolve SLA continues to run... The SLA clock for resolution ends only when the state is set to Resolved.

questions.question: Which roles provide the ability to create, update, and resolve incidents? (Select two)

explanation.correct: The ITIL role enables an individual to create, update, and resolve incidents while providing read-write access to the CMDB. The ITIL_admin role can perform additional tasks including closing and deleting incidents. The sn_incident_read role only provides read access.

wrongAnswers.explanation: sn_incident_read provides read-only access to incidents, not write capabilities
incident_viewer is not a standard ServiceNow incident role

source.excerpt: The ITIL role enables an individual to create, update, and resolve incidents while also providing read-write access to the CMDB... anyone with the ITIL admin role can perform tasks such as creating, updating, closing, and deleting incidents and related records.

questions.question: What happens to child incidents when a parent incident is marked as Resolved?

options.text: Child incidents remain in their current state
Child incidents are also set to Resolved
Child incidents are moved to On Hold

explanation.correct: When a parent incident is marked as Resolved, the same status is applied to all child incidents. Additionally, any notes, codes, comments, or work notes associated with the parent incident are automatically duplicated in the child incidents.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Child incidents follow the parent's state changes, they don't remain independent
Child incidents are not deleted; they follow the parent's state
Child incidents are set to Resolved, not On Hold, when the parent is resolved

source.excerpt: Whenever a parent incident is marked as resolved, the same status is applied to all child incidents. Additionally, any notes, codes, comments, or work notes associated with the parent incident are automatically duplicated in the child incidents.

questions.question: What is the default time period for an incident to remain in the Resolved state before automatically closing?

explanation.correct: The standard default time for an incident to remain in a Resolved state is 7 days. If the user takes no action within this time frame, the incident will automatically be closed. This can be configured to meet specific organizational needs.

wrongAnswers.explanation: 24 hours is too short; the default is 7 days
3 days is not the default; the default is 7 days
14 days is longer than the default 7-day period

source.excerpt: Within the platform, the standard time for an incident to remain in a resolved state is seven days. If the user takes no action within this time frame, the incident will automatically be closed.

questions.question: A user reports they cannot access an application. Investigation reveals all users are affected because an application job is hung. What should Incident Management focus on?

options.text: Determine why the job hung and prevent recurrence
Remove the hung job so users can access the application
Create a Problem record and wait for root cause analysis
Escalate to Change Management for a permanent fix

explanation.correct: Incident Management focuses on restoring service quickly. In this case, removing the hung job will restore access. Determining why the job hung and preventing recurrence is the focus of Problem Management, not Incident Management.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Determining root cause and prevention is Problem Management's responsibility, not Incident Management
While a Problem may be created, Incident Management shouldn't wait for root cause analysis before restoring service
Immediate service restoration is the priority; Change Management may be involved later for permanent fixes

source.excerpt: Incident management focuses on removing the hung job so that users can access the application again. Its focus is not to determine why the job hung and what to do to ensure it doesn't happen again, as that is the focus of problem management.

questions.question: What does the SLA Timeline indicator color RED signify?

options.text: The task SLA is below 50% of defined duration
The task SLA is between 75% and 100%
The task has exceeded the defined SLA duration

explanation.correct: A task will be indicated in red if it exceeds the defined SLA duration (breached). Green is below 50%, yellow is 50-75%, orange is 75-100%, and gray indicates the task is paused.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Below 50% is indicated by green, not red
75-100% is indicated by orange, not red
Paused tasks are indicated in gray, not red

source.excerpt: Green indicates a task SLA stage that is below 50% of the defined SLA duration. Yellow represents a stage between 50% and 75%. And orange represents a stage between 75% and 100% A task will be indicated in red if it exceeds the defined SLA duration.

questions.question: Which of the following are characteristics of Major Incidents? (Select two)

options.text: They exceed the standard priority matrix
They always require Change Management approval
They impact a significant number of users
They can only be created manually

explanation.correct: Major incidents exceed the standard priority matrix and have the greatest impact and urgency. They impact a significant number of users and deprive the business of vital services. They can be created by automated trigger rules or manually.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Major incidents don't require Change approval to be created, though changes may be needed for resolution
Major incidents can be generated by automated trigger rules or manual creation

source.excerpt: Major incidents are those that exceed the standard priority matrix and have the greatest impact and urgency. They impact a significant number of users and deprive the business of one or more vital services... Automated trigger rules or manual creation can generate major incidents.

questions.question: What happens to the SLA clock when an incident is placed On Hold?

options.text: The SLA clock is permanently stopped
The SLA clock may be paused
The SLA is canceled and a new one begins

explanation.correct: The SLA clock may be paused when the state is set to On Hold. The agent must reset the state to In Progress to restart the SLA clock. Whether it pauses depends on the SLA configuration.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The SLA clock may pause on On Hold, depending on configuration
The clock is paused, not permanently stopped; it resumes when state changes to In Progress
The SLA is not canceled on On Hold; it may be paused but continues from where it left off

source.excerpt: The SLA clock may be paused when the state is set to On Hold. In such cases, the agent must reset the state to In Progress to restart the SLA clock.

questions.question: A parent incident is reopened by the end user after it was closed. What happens to the child incidents?

options.text: Child incidents are also reopened and set to In Progress
Child incidents are set to On Hold

explanation.correct: When a parent incident is reopened by the end user, the parent state is set to In Progress, but the child incidents remain closed. This is an exception to the normal parent-child behavior where changes to the parent typically affect children.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Unlike most parent-child behaviors, when reopened by the end user, only the parent changes to In Progress
Child incidents are not deleted; they simply remain closed
Child incidents remain closed, not moved to On Hold

source.excerpt: In case the parent incident is reopened by the end user, its state is set to in-progress, but the child incidents remain closed.

questions.question: Which field should be used to communicate with affected users about incident status updates?

explanation.correct: The Additional Comments field is used for customer-facing communication. Support teams can communicate with users through this field, and it triggers email notifications. Work notes are only visible to internal users.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Work notes can only be viewed by internal users, not customers
Short description is for describing the incident, not for ongoing communication
Resolution notes are for documenting the final resolution, not ongoing updates

source.excerpt: This field can only be viewed by internal users. However, support teams may occasionally contact affected users for additional information or to provide updates. Support teams can communicate with users through the Additional Comments field.

questions.question: Which methods can be used to create an incident in ServiceNow? (Choose three.)

options.text: Record Producers in the Service Catalog

explanation.correct: Incidents can be created via Record Producers in the Service Catalog (which copy user input to auto-populate incident fields), Virtual Agent conversations, Walk-up Experience (when unresolved at walk-up location), phone calls to service desk, Universal Request, and third-party integrations.

wrongAnswers.explanation: ServiceNow does not support direct SQL insertion. Records are created through the platform's APIs, forms, or automation tools.
Modifying the CMDB schema has no relation to incident creation. The CMDB stores configuration items, not incidents.

references: ITSM Fundamentals course - Incident Management Creation and Classification

source.excerpt: It also can be created using a virtual agent or an integration with a third party tool.

questions.question: What color does the SLA Timeline indicator display when a task SLA is between 50% and 75% of the defined duration?

explanation.correct: Yellow represents a task SLA stage between 50% and 75% of the defined SLA duration. Green is below 50%, orange is 75-100%, and red indicates a breached SLA (exceeds 100%).

wrongAnswers.explanation: Green indicates a task SLA stage that is below 50% of the defined SLA duration.
Orange represents a stage between 75% and 100% of the defined SLA duration.
Red indicates that the task has exceeded (breached) the defined SLA duration.

references: ITSM Fundamentals course - Incident Management Creation and Classification

source.excerpt: Yellow represents a stage between 50% and 75%. And orange represents a stage between 75% and 100%.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a valid incident state in ServiceNow?

explanation.correct: Assessed is a state used in Problem Management, not Incident Management. Valid incident states are: New, In Progress, On Hold, Resolved, Closed, and Canceled.

wrongAnswers.explanation: In Progress is a valid incident state indicating the incident has been assigned and is under investigation.
On Hold is a valid incident state indicating the investigation is paused to gather additional information.
Canceled is a valid incident state for duplicate, unnecessary, or non-incident records.

references: ITSM Fundamentals course - Incident Management Creation and Classification

source.excerpt: Whenever a new incident is reported, it starts in a new state... Various options are available for new incidents: in progress, on hold, resolved, closed, canceled.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about Incident Management communication are true?
a) Work Notes are visible only to internal users.
b) Additional Comments trigger email notifications to the caller.
c) The Activity section records all state changes, emails, and attachments.
d) Work Notes automatically notify the caller about investigation progress.

explanation.correct: Statements a, b, and c are true. Work Notes are internal-only, Additional Comments communicate with users (triggering notifications), and the Activity/Notes tab records all changes. Statement d is false — Work Notes do NOT notify the caller; they are internal communication only.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Statement d is false. Work Notes are for internal use and do not automatically notify the caller.
Statement a is also true — Work Notes are visible only to internal users.
Statement b is also true — Additional Comments do trigger notifications to affected users.

references: ITSM Fundamentals course - Incident Management Investigation and Resolution

source.excerpt: This field can only be viewed by internal users... Support teams can communicate with users through the Additional Comments field.

questions.question: Which two plugins must be activated to enable Universal Request integration for Incident Management? (Choose two.)

options.text: sn_inc_uni_req (Universal Request Integration for Incident Management)

explanation.correct: To integrate Universal Request with Incident Management, you must activate both the sn_uni_req (Universal Request) plugin and the sn_inc_uni_req (Universal Request Integration for Incident Management) plugin.

wrongAnswers.explanation: sn_incident_write is an ITSM roles plugin for granular incident access, not related to Universal Request integration.
sn_itsm_workspace is the workspace plugin, not related to Universal Request integration.

references: ITSM Fundamentals course - Incident Management Creation and Classification

source.excerpt: To activate this feature, be sure to activate both the universal request, sn_uni_req and the universal request integration for incident management sn_inc_uni_req plugins.

questions.question: An incident has a Priority 3 and the SLA clock is running. The priority is changed to Priority 1. What happens to the SLA?

options.text: The previous SLA is canceled and a new one begins, but the SLA clock does not reset
The previous SLA is canceled and a new one begins with the clock reset to zero
Both SLAs run simultaneously until the incident is resolved

explanation.correct: When the priority of an incident changes, the previous SLA is canceled and a new one begins. However, the SLA clock does not reset — it continues from where it was. This ensures elapsed time is tracked accurately.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The SLA does change when priority changes — the old one is canceled and a new one starts.
While a new SLA begins, the clock does not reset to zero — elapsed time carries forward.
Only one SLA runs at a time — the previous one is canceled before the new one starts.

references: ITSM Fundamentals course - Incident Management Creation and Classification

source.excerpt: If the priority of the incident changes, the previous SLA is canceled and a new one begins. However, the SLA clock does not reset in this scenario.

questions.question: Which role holds the authority to manage incident properties and trigger major incident workflows?

explanation.correct: The incident_manager role holds the authority to manage properties and trigger major incident roles. The ITIL role enables creating/updating/resolving incidents, and itil_admin adds closing/deleting capabilities.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The ITIL role enables creating, updating, and resolving incidents but cannot manage properties or trigger major incident workflows.
The itil_admin role can create, update, close, and delete incidents, but does not manage incident properties or major incident workflows.
sn_incident_write is a granular access role from the ITSM roles plugin, not related to incident management or major incident workflows.

references: ITSM Fundamentals course - Incident Management Creation and Classification

source.excerpt: The incident manager holds the authority to manage properties and trigger major incident roles.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the Incident Communications Management application?

options.text: To assign incidents to the correct support groups
To manage and streamline communication during major incidents
To automatically resolve incidents based on knowledge articles
To generate SLA reports for incident resolution times

explanation.correct: The Incident Communications Management application is designed to manage communication during major incidents effectively. It allows creating communication plans, assigning contact responsibilities, sending SMS/voicemail notifications, setting up conference calls, and enabling self-service users to subscribe to incident communication plans.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Incident assignment is handled through the normal incident lifecycle, not the Communications Management application.
Agent Assist and knowledge search help find relevant articles, but don't automatically resolve incidents.
SLA reporting is handled through Performance Analytics and reporting features, not the Communications Management application.

references: ITSM Fundamentals course - Incident Management Creation and Classification

source.excerpt: The incident communication management framework is designed to manage communication during a major incident effectively.
